The `mix` function with `sign(t)` handles this by preferring the camera position if $t \le 0$ [S1, unofficial].

The code snippet in Source [S1] defines the function `getCloserPos` which uses `mix(camera, frontFaceIntersection, useFrontCoord)`. The variable `useFrontCoord` is calculated as `0.5 + 0.5 * sign(t)`. When `t <= 0`, `sign(t)` is either -1 or 0. If `t < 0`, `sign(t) = -1`, so `useFrontCoord = 0`. If `t = 0`, `sign(t) = 0`, so `useFrontCoord = 0.5`. In both cases, the mix function favors the camera position (weight 1.0 or 0.5 respectively) over the front face intersection. The text description also explicitly states: 'if t is negative or zero (camera inside), use the camera position.' Thus, the evidence supports the claim.
